messages:
maya: Heads-up: huge slowdown on console charts after telemetry-v2 landed in canary. First paint blocked ~500ms, lots of GC.

jorge: Repro'd on my laptop. Network shows a single ~1.1MB telemetry blob for /dash/overview.

ken: Any stack traces? looks like a big synchronous parse.

maya: Console shows RangeError from parseFullContext + long main-thread task.

samir: That matches the change that started shipping full event context for correlation. We accidentally flipped sampling to 100% for dashboard reads in config.

ops-bot: deployment telemetry/v2-canary -> 10% at 1740009000.

maya: Dashboards unusable for canary users. Can we reduce traffic or rollback?

jorge: I can scale the canary to 0 now. Suggestion before rollback: try lazy-loading the chart bundle and offloading JSON.parse to a worker as a mitigation.

ken: Worker parse is feasible quickly. StructuredClone may add overhead but better than blocking main thread. Streaming parse would be ideal but slower to ship.

samir: We should fix server-side too: gate full-event-context with per-route quotas so dashboard reads default to sampled context. Example: /dash/* fullContextRate 0.02.

maya: I've rolled canary to 0 at 1740009300. ops-bot: rollback executed.

ops-bot: rollback telemetry/v2-canary -> 0% at 1740009300 (initiated by maya).

jorge: After rollback, dashboards render normally for me.

ken: I'll open a small PR implementing worker-based parse + lazy chart import behind a feature flag. If perf looks good we'll enable and then re-rollout telemetry change.

samir: I'll write an RFC for telemetry sampling policy + add a telemetry.parse_ms perf counter so canary alerts trigger next time.

maya: Action items: ken prototype, samir RFC + perf counter, ops keep canary at 0 until we have metrics. Closing thread unless new fallout appears.
